---
title: "Units, Parameters, and Optimization"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## CONVERGING concept

This page explains the current candidate design. It does not define units,
parameter schemas, objective formulas, optimizer controls, or failure
behavior; the linked contracts remain the sole authority.
:::

## Design pressure

Reusable physical models need values that retain their declared units and
calibration meaning, yet equivalent representations must identify the same
compiled request. Optimization adds another boundary: a component author may
publish a parameter without silently choosing every model's search envelope or
every consumer's target.

## Selected abstraction {#parameter-vs-optimization-variable}

SCNSim uses one Quantity registry and a canonical SI identity for physical
values. A sealed Plan supplies baselines; an immutable `ParameterSet` supplies
an explicit operation variant. A Composite deliberately exposes its supported
`ParameterRef` objects, including any identity fan-out or calibrated mapping.

Parameter ownership is divided deliberately: the Library author owns schema
and calibration context, the circuit-model author owns reusable optimization
recipes, and the Notebook consumer owns a Design Target and any explicit,
immutable departure from that recipe. Unit conversion, optimizer coordinates,
objective normalization, and numerical conditioning remain separate concerns.

## Problem solved

This preserves physical identity across display units and keeps a parameter
variant attached to the request that used it. It also makes optimization
reusable without hiding targets, bounds, or calibration assumptions inside a
component, and prevents a numerical representation choice from being mistaken
for a physical model change or an acceptance rule.

## Intentionally not owned

This concept does not create a second unit type system, accept bare physical
numbers, or let a `ParameterSet` change a Ref lineage. It does not assign a
Design Target, optimization Gate, universal bounds, or automatic public
linear-algebra scaling configuration.
